chunks: And in it, that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted and Glorified, did not grant Satan authority over the believers except over those who follow him.

And He made for them partners in their [own] selves to mislead them in knowledge. And for Satan there was no authority over those who believed and put their trust in their Lord. They were [thus] Muslims [submitting to Allah].

key_terms.يَئُوسُوا: He can make them lose hope/despair

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for Satan having authority over believers according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights this conditional authority (*sultan*) to refute the Mu'tazila and Khawarij extremes, establishing that Satan's power is not intrinsic but derived from human choice. This narration underscores the Shia doctrine of free will, where believers retain agency to either submit to Satan's whispers or remain steadfast through sincere *iman*, thereby nullifying his claim over them.
